proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(C_v<\infty\), and write \(c_{ax}=p_xe_{ax}\).  The stipulated spaces of \(p\) and \(e\) give \(c_{ax}>0\) for every one of the finitely many cells.  Choose two distinct support values \(y_u\ne y_w\), which exist because the elements of \(\mathcal Y\) are distinct and \(L\ge3\).  For any probability vector \(q_{ax}\), direct expansion of the variance gives
\[
 \sigma^2_{ax}(q)
 =\sum_{\ell<m}q_{ax\ell}q_{axm}(y_\ell-y_m)^2.
\tag{1}
\]
Thus \(q^0_{ax\ell}\ge\eta\), by \(\mathrm{ass:eta\text{-}interior}\), implies
\[
 \underline\sigma^2:=\eta^2(y_u-y_w)^2
 \le \sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)\le 4C_Y^2.
\tag{2}
\]
The upper inequality follows from \(|Y-EY|\le2C_Y\).  For \(z\in\mathbb R^d\), the definition of \(\Sigma(r)\) yields
\[
 z^\top\Sigma(r)z
 =\sum_{x=1}^K\sum_{a=0}^1
 \frac{p_x\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)}{e_{ax}r_{ax}}(z^\top d_x)^2.
\tag{3}
\]
Because \(r_{ax}\in[\rho,1]\), all coefficients in (3) have fixed positive lower and finite upper bounds.  Moreover, \(\operatorname{rank}(F)=d\) by \(\mathrm{ass:menu\text{-}rank}\), and multiplication by the positive diagonal matrix \(\operatorname{diag}(p)\) does not change row rank, so \(d_1,\ldots,d_K\) span \(\mathbb R^d\).  The continuous function \(z\mapsto\sum_x(z^\top d_x)^2\) therefore has a positive minimum on the Euclidean unit sphere.  Equations (2)--(3) consequently place \(\{\Sigma(r):r\in\mathcal R_B\}\) in a fixed compact subset \(\mathcal K\subset\mathbb S_{++}^d\).

We next construct the pilot objective and prove its uniform accuracy under the weakened pilot condition.  Put
\[
 b_n=m_n^{-1/4}+n^{-1/2},\qquad t_n=b_n^{1/2}.
\tag{4}
\]
The replacement \(\mathrm{ass:pilot\text{-}rate}\) says \(m_n\to\infty\); hence \(b_n\to0\), \(t_n\to0\), and
\[
 \frac{b_n}{t_n}=b_n^{1/2}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{5}
\]
Let \(N_{ax}\) be the number of fully labelled pilot records in cell \((a,x)\), and let \(\widehat\nu_{s,ax}\) be the within-cell average of \(Y^s\), for \(s=1,2\), with an arbitrary value in \([-C_Y^s,C_Y^s]\) when \(N_{ax}=0\).  If \(\nu_{s,ax,n}=E_{q_n(h,v)}(Y^s\mid A=a,X=x)\), then
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\!\left(\frac{N_{ax}}{m_n}\right)\le\frac{c_{ax}}{m_n},
 \qquad
 E\!\left[\left\{\frac1{m_n}\sum_{i=1}^{m_n}
 \mathbf1\{X_i=x,A_i=a\}(Y_i^s-\nu_{s,ax,n})\right\}^2\right]
 \le\frac{c_{ax}C_s^2}{m_n},
\tag{6}
\]
where \(C_s=2C_Y^s\).  The elementary implication
\(\mathbf1\{|U|>t\}\le U^2/t^2\), followed by expectation, turns (6) into
\[
 \sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\ \lVert v\rVert\le C_v}
 P_{q_n(h,v)}\!\left(
 |\widehat\nu_{s,ax}-\nu_{s,ax,n}|>C_{ax,s}m_n^{-1/4}
 \right)=O(m_n^{-1/2}).
\tag{7}
\]
Indeed, the same inequality first gives \(P(N_{ax}<m_nc_{ax}/2)=O(m_n^{-1})\); on its complement the centered numerator in (6), divided by \(N_{ax}/m_n\ge c_{ax}/2\), gives (7).  The constants do not depend on \((h,v)\), because only the fixed bounds on \(Y\) and the fixed cell probabilities \(c_{ax}\) were used.  A union bound over the fixed \(4K\) moment coordinates gives events \(E_n(C_v)\) such that
\[
 \inf_{h\in\mathcal H,\ \lVert v\rVert\le C_v}
 P_{q_n(h,v)}\{E_n(C_v)\}\longrightarrow1.
\tag{8}
\]

Linearity of \(s(h,v)=S_0h+Wv\), compactness of \(\mathcal H\), and boundedness of \(\{v:\lVert v\rVert\le C_v\}\) imply a finite constant \(D(C_v)\) with \(\sup_{h,v}\lVert s(h,v)\rVert_\infty\le D(C_v)\).  Since \(q_n-q^0=s(h,v)/\sqrt n\) and the support is finite,
\[
 \max_{a,x,s\in\{1,2\}}
 |\nu_{s,ax,n}-\nu_{s,ax,0}|\le C(C_v)n^{-1/2}.
\tag{9}
\]
The variance map \((\nu_1,\nu_2)\mapsto\nu_2-\nu_1^2\) is Lipschitz on the bounded moment rectangle.  Therefore, after clipping the pilot variance estimates to \([\underline\sigma^2/2,4C_Y^2]\), (7)--(9) imply on \(E_n(C_v)\)
\[
 \max_{a,x}|\widehat\sigma^2_{ax}-\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)|\le C_0(C_v)b_n.
\tag{10}
\]
This is the only pilot-moment event needed for design selection, and its proof used \(m_n\to\infty\), not any comparison of \(m_n\) with \(\sqrt n\).

Let \(\widehat\Sigma_n(r)\) be the formula for \(\Sigma(r)\) with \(\widehat\sigma^2_{ax}\) in place of \(\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)\), and let \(\widehat L_n(r)\) be the corresponding Gaussian minimax value.  Since \(r_{ax}\ge\rho\), (10) gives
\[
 \sup_{r\in\mathcal R_B}\lVert\widehat\Sigma_n(r)-\Sigma(r)\rVert
 \le C_1(C_v)b_n.
\tag{11}
\]
For \(S,S'\) in a sufficiently small fixed compact enlargement of \(\mathcal K\), differentiate the centered normal density along \(S_u=(1-u)S+uS'\).  The derivative identity
\[
 \frac{d}{du}\phi_{S_u}(z)
 =\frac12\phi_{S_u}(z)
 \left[z^\top S_u^{-1}(S'-S)S_u^{-1}z
       -\operatorname{tr}\{S_u^{-1}(S'-S)\}\right]
\tag{12}
\]
and the common positive lower and finite upper eigenvalue bounds imply, after integration in \(z\) and \(u\),
\[
 \sup_{h\in\mathbb R^d}
 \operatorname{TV}\{N(h,S),N(h,S')\}
 \le C_2\lVert S-S'\rVert.
\tag{13}
\]
The regret is bounded by
\(R_H=2\sup_{h\in\mathcal H}\lVert h\rVert_\infty<\infty\).  Hence, for every rule \(\delta\) and state \(h\), changing \(S\) to \(S'\) changes expected regret by at most \(R_H\) times (13).  Taking the supremum over \(h\), then the infimum over \(\delta\), in both directions proves from (11)
\[
 \sup_{r\in\mathcal R_B}|\widehat L_n(r)-L(r)|
 \le C_3(C_v)b_n
 \quad\text{on }E_n(C_v).
\tag{14}
\]

We now give the measurable nested-cell selector.  Set \(k_n=\lfloor\log_2\log(n+2)\rfloor\).  Through depth \(k_n\), use exactly the coordinate order, parent-only recursion, closed-child convention, and lexicographic order in \(\mathrm{def:implementation\text{-}handle}\).  For each nonempty feasible part of a child of the currently selected parent, approximate its minimum \(\widehat L_n\)-value with deterministic error at most \(b_n\).  Such approximations can be constructed by successively refining finite state nets, Gaussian observation rectangles, and the projected design nets supplied by \(P_B\).  To see that the design nets also work on boundary cells, first note that continuity of \(P_B\), its identity action on \(\mathcal R_B\), and density of the ambient full-box nets make their projected images dense in \(\mathcal R_B\).  If \(C=\mathcal R_B\cap D\) is a nonempty closed child cell, send every projected net point \(g\) to its Euclidean nearest point \(c_C(g)\in C\).  Existence follows from compactness; uniqueness follows because \(C\) is convex and squared Euclidean distance is strictly convex.  If \(c\in C\) and \(\lVert g-c\rVert\le\xi\), then
\[
 \lVert c_C(g)-c\rVert
 \le\lVert c_C(g)-g\rVert+\lVert g-c\rVert\le2\xi,
\]
so these cell projections form refining finite nets even when \(C\) is a singleton or lies wholly on a dyadic boundary.  For effectively represented instances, \(\mathrm{thm:certified\text{-}computation}\), applied after appending the child's rational box inequalities, gives terminating outward certificates.  For any fixed mathematical instance, deterministic simple-function approximations give the same existence conclusion without asserting an effective stopping rule: (12)--(13) give uniform covariance continuity and compactness of \(\mathcal H\) gives finite state nets.  Every finite-stage operation is a Gaussian rectangle integral, a finite sum, a cell projection, or a finite linear program.  The child index is finite at each stage; resolving its finitely many ties lexicographically makes the resulting map of the pilot moments Borel measurable.

For clarity, the game approximation used here is uniform rather than pointwise.  Differentiating a Gaussian density in its mean, by the same calculation as (12), gives a constant \(C_5\), uniform over the compact covariance family, such that
\[
 \operatorname{TV}\{N(h,S),N(h',S)\}\le C_5\lVert h-h'\rVert.
\]
Since \(h\mapsto\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}(h,j)\) is Lipschitz uniformly over \(j\in[M]\), and the Gaussian law is likewise Lipschitz in its mean on the compact state set, every rule's risk has one common modulus of continuity in \(h\).  Thus replacing \(\mathcal H\) by a sufficiently fine finite net changes every worst-state risk by a uniformly vanishing amount.  For a finite state net and a finite covariance net, let \(\mu\) be the sum of the finitely many Gaussian laws involved.  Rational rectangles generate the Borel sigma-field, so each component of any measurable simplex-valued rule has rectangle-simple approximants converging in \(L^1(\mu)\); projecting their vector of values onto \(\Delta_M\) preserves measurability and changes the finite collection of risks by a quantity tending to zero.  A covariance net and (13) extend this approximation uniformly over \(\mathcal K\).  Taking a rule within an arbitrary positive amount of the defining infimum of \(L\) proves that the finite rectangle games converge uniformly to the Gaussian games.  This justifies both the deterministic cell-value accuracy and the finite linear-program representation asserted above.

Let \(\widehat v_{n,j,b}\) be the resulting approximate value of feasible child \(b\) at depth \(j\), and, when the parent is \(\mathcal D_{j-1}^\dagger\), let
\[
 v_{j,b}=\min_{r\in\mathcal R_B\cap D_{j,b}}L(r).
\]
Equation (14) and the deterministic numerical tolerance give a deterministic
\(\alpha_n=C_4(C_v)b_n\) such that, on \(E_n(C_v)\),
\[
 |\widehat v_{n,j,b}-v_{j,b}|\le\alpha_n
\tag{15}
\]
simultaneously for every child tested through depth \(k_n\).  By (4)--(5), \(\alpha_n=o(t_n)\).  Retain precisely the siblings satisfying
\[
 \widehat v_{n,j,b}\le\min_c\widehat v_{n,j,c}+t_n,
\tag{16}
\]
and select the lexicographically first retained child.  A sibling attaining the finite approximated minimum is always retained, so all empirical cells are nonempty; the parent-only recursion makes them nested.

For the feasible children of the population parent \(\mathcal D_{j-1}^\dagger\), define
\[
 E_j=\{b:v_{j,b}=V^*\},\qquad
 \gamma_j(L)=
 \begin{cases}
 \min_{b\notin E_j}\{v_{j,b}-V^*\},&
 E_j\text{ is not the set of all feasible children},\\
 +\infty,&E_j\text{ is the set of all feasible children}.
 \end{cases}
\tag{17}
\]
At least one child is in \(E_j\): the finitely many closed children cover the selected parent cell, which contains a minimizer by the definitions of \(\mathcal D_{j-1}^\dagger\) and \(\mathcal C_{j-1}^\dagger\).  Each feasible child is compact, and continuity of \(L\), which also follows from (13) and the continuous covariance formula, makes its displayed minimum attained.  Consequently every ineligible child has value strictly above \(V^*\); finiteness of the sibling set gives \(\gamma_j(L)>0\).

Suppose inductively that the empirical parent at depth \(j-1\) is \(\mathcal D_{j-1}^\dagger\).  By (15), every child in \(E_j\) lies within \(2\alpha_n\) of the smallest empirical value and is retained if \(2\alpha_n<t_n\).  Every child outside \(E_j\) lies at least \(\gamma_j(L)-2\alpha_n\) above the smallest empirical value and is rejected if
\[
 t_n+2\alpha_n<\gamma_j(L).
\tag{18}
\]
Under these inequalities the retained set equals \(E_j\), so its lexicographically first element is exactly \(\mathcal D_j^\dagger\).  Induction proves stabilization of every fixed prefix.  If a population minimizer is on a shared dyadic boundary, every closed child containing it is separately feasible and belongs to \(E_j\); (16) retains all such children before the same lexicographic convention is applied.  Disconnected, flat, or tied minimizing sets merely enlarge \(E_j\).  Thus the argument includes both separated tied minima and dyadic-boundary minima, establishing the stated early-kill property.

The outward cell bounds in \(\mathrm{thm:certified\text{-}computation}\), or the same deterministic convergent bounds for a fixed instance, eventually give a positive lower certificate for every positive gap in (17).  Let \(j_n(L)\) be the largest \(j\le k_n\) for which the certified lower gap bounds exceed \(2t_n\) at every level \(1\le i\le j\), with \(j_n(L)=0\) if none is certified.  This definition depends only on the schedule and the population prefix-separation profile, not on \(C_v\).  For each fixed \(C_v\), (5) implies that eventually \(2\alpha_n<t_n\), so \(2t_n<\gamma_i(L)\) implies (18).  Every finite minimum \(\min_{i\le j}\gamma_i(L)\) is positive, whereas \(k_n\to\infty\) and \(t_n\to0\).  Hence
\[
 j_n(L)\longrightarrow\infty,
 \qquad
 a_n(L):=\sup_{m\ge n}2^{-j_m(L)}\downarrow0.
\tag{19}
\]
On \(E_n(C_v)\), the empirical and population paths agree through depth \(j_n(L)\).  Choose the final feasible point of a selected cell by successively minimizing its coordinates over that compact cell; since the cell indices form a countable discrete set, this is a measurable fixed lookup.  Both this point \(\widehat r_n\) and \(r^\dagger\) lie in the same depth-\(j_n(L)\) population cell, even if later empirical descendants select another minimizing branch within it.  The dyadic diameter bound gives
\[
 \lVert\widehat r_n-r^\dagger\rVert
 \le\sqrt{2K}(1-\rho)2^{-j_n(L)}
 \le\sqrt{2K}(1-\rho)a_n(L).
\tag{20}
\]
Combining (8), (19), and (20) proves locally uniform convergence and
\(\lVert\widehat r_n-r^\dagger\rVert=O_P\{a_n(L)\}\).  The sequence is necessarily schedule- and law-specific through \(b_n\) and the prefix gaps \(\gamma_j(L)\).

It remains to couple this design selector to the terminal rule.  At deterministic refinement level \(s\), use the pilot covariance \(\widehat\Sigma_n(\widehat r_n)\), take a finite state net, a rational observation-rectangle partition after tail truncation, and solve the resulting finite primal--dual Gaussian game to total error at most \(2^{-s}\); resolve all finite ties lexicographically.  The construction in \(\mathrm{thm:certified\text{-}computation}\) supplies these objects on represented instances, and the deterministic refinements just used supply them for the fixed mathematical instance.  Let \(J_s<\infty\) be the number of rectangles.  A diagonal sequence \(s_n\uparrow\infty\) can be chosen sufficiently slowly that
\[
 J_{s_n}n^{-1/2}\longrightarrow0,
\tag{21}
\]
while its state-mesh, tail, quadrature, rounding, covariance, and finite-game errors all tend to zero.  Because each level uses finitely many Borel pilot statistics and lexicographic comparisons, this rectangle-constant rule is jointly measurable with \(\widehat r_n\).

For the distributional coupling, let \(\beta_n=\beta(q_n(h,v))\), \(b=\beta_n-\widehat\beta\), and, conditional on \(\mathscr P_n\), define
\[
 H_{i,ax}=\frac{\mathbf1\{X_i=x,A_i=a,R_i=1\}}
 {p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
 (Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-\widehat\beta_{ax}).
\tag{22}
\]
Annotation ignorability gives \(E(H_i\mid\mathscr P_n)=b\).  The summands \(A_{\mathrm{map}}(H_i-b)\) are conditionally centered and uniformly bounded, because \(|Y|\le C_Y\), \(\widehat\beta\) is clipped to the convex hull of \(\mathcal Y\), \(p_xe_{ax}>0\), and \(\widehat r_{n,ax}\ge\rho\).  Only one coordinate of \(H_i\) can be nonzero, so direct multiplication gives their exact covariance
\[
 S_n=A_{\mathrm{map}}\left[
 \operatorname{diag}_{a,x}\left\{
 \frac{\sigma^2_{ax}(q_n)+b_{ax}^2}
 {p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
 \right\}-bb^\top\right]A_{\mathrm{map}}^\top.
\tag{23}
\]
The last two terms inside the brackets,
\(\operatorname{diag}\{b_{ax}^2/(p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax})\}-bb^\top\), form a covariance matrix and are positive semidefinite.  Applying the same second-moment calculation as in (6) to the pilot cell means yields, locally uniformly,
\[
 \lVert b\rVert=O_P(m_n^{-1/2}).
\tag{24}
\]
The affine chart gives
\(\max_{a,x}|\sigma^2_{ax}(q_n)-\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)|=O(n^{-1/2})\) uniformly on the bounded fiber.  Inserting the columns \(-p_xd_x\) and \(p_xd_x\) of \(A_{\mathrm{map}}=[-F\;F]\) shows exactly that
\[
 A_{\mathrm{map}}\operatorname{diag}_{a,x}\left\{
 \frac{\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)}{p_xe_{ax}r_{ax}}
 \right\}A_{\mathrm{map}}^\top=\Sigma(r).
\tag{25}
\]
Equations (20), (23)--(25), the annotation floor, and continuity of \(r\mapsto1/r\) on \([\rho,1]\) imply
\[
 \lVert S_n-\Sigma(r^\dagger)\rVert
 =O_P(m_n^{-1}+n^{-1/2}+a_n(L))=o_P(1)
\tag{26}
\]
locally uniformly.  This is where pilot estimation enters the covariance: mere \(m_n^{-1}\to0\) suffices.

By (2), the uniform \(O(n^{-1/2})\) variance perturbation from \(q^0\) to \(q_n\), and the rank argument following (3), \(S_n\) has a common positive lower eigenvalue with probability tending to one uniformly on the bounded fiber.  Normalize the \(n\) summands in
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_p(q_n(h,v))\}
 =\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^nA_{\mathrm{map}}(H_i-b)
\tag{27}
\]
by \(S_n^{-1/2}\).  Uniform boundedness makes the sum of their third Euclidean absolute moments \(O(n^{-1/2})\).  The frozen result \(\mathrm{lem:bentkus\text{-}convex\text{-}set}\) therefore bounds the conditional probability error of each observation rectangle by \(O(n^{-1/2})\).  Summing over the \(J_{s_n}\) rectangles and using (21), then using (26) and the Gaussian total-variation bound (13), gives
\[
 \sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\ \lVert v\rVert\le C_v}
 |\operatorname{Risk}_n(h,v)-\operatorname{Risk}_{G,n}(h,v)|=o(1).
\tag{28}
\]
Here \(\operatorname{Risk}_{G,n}(h,v)\) is the risk of the same rectangle rule when its input has law \(N(\sqrt n\,\theta_p(q_n(h,v)),\Sigma(r^\dagger))\); the downstream attainment proof supplies the already established identification of this mean with \(h\).  Bounded regret turns the locally uniform conditional convergence in probability into unconditional convergence.  This proves the jointly refined Gaussian-rule risk coupling.  The separate condition \(m_n/n\to0\) in \(\mathrm{ass:pilot\text{-}vanishes}\) also keeps the pilot likelihood negligible in \(\mathrm{thm:nuisance\text{-}uniform\text{-}experiment}\); no stronger pilot growth is used.

Finally, the claimed limitation is only generic.  For any \(\epsilon>0\), define on \([0,1]\)
\[
 f_+(z)=\epsilon z,\qquad f_-(z)=\epsilon(1-z),\qquad g(z)=\epsilon/2.
\tag{29}
\]
The unique canonical minimizers of \(f_+\) and \(f_-\) are zero and one, while
\[
 \lVert g-f_+\rVert_\infty=\lVert g-f_-\rVert_\infty=\epsilon/2.
\tag{30}
\]
Any selector seeing only the common approximation \(g\) returns the same \(z_g\) in the two cases, and
\[
 \max\{|z_g|,|z_g-1|\}\ge\frac12.
\tag{31}
\]
Letting \(\epsilon\downarrow0\) proves that continuity plus uniform objective-approximation control alone gives no spatial recovery modulus tending to zero uniformly over all continuous objectives.  Because (29) is not asserted to lie in the Gaussian-risk family \(r\mapsto L(r)\), this establishes no model-specific impossibility, exactly as claimed.

Use the jointly measurable construction proved in \(\mathrm{thm:coupled\text{-}measurable\text{-}attainment}\): fully label the independent pilot, select \(\widehat r_n\in\mathcal R_B\), annotate each main-wave outcome independently at its selected cell rate, compute \(\widetilde\theta_n\), and apply the coupled rectangle-constant Gaussian rule to \(\sqrt n\,\widetilde\theta_n\).  Feasibility holds sample by sample.  The replacement \(\mathrm{ass:pilot\text{-}rate}\) gives \(m_n\to\infty\), while \(\mathrm{ass:pilot\text{-}vanishes}\) gives \(m_n/n\to0\).  The former is enough for the design and nuisance estimates, and the latter makes the pilot likelihood asymptotically negligible in \(\mathrm{thm:nuisance\text{-}uniform\text{-}experiment}\).  Together with \(\widehat r_n\to r^\dagger\), these facts put the constructed sequence \(\mathcal A^*\) in \(\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{det}}\).  The prescribed coordinate order, parent-only recursion, separate testing of shared-boundary children, stabilization of every fixed prefix, and the rate \(O_P\{a_n(L)\}\) follow directly from the coupled theorem.

We verify the estimator limit and its precise pilot requirement.  Fix \(C_v<\infty\), and define
\[
 c_{ax}=p_xe_{ax},\qquad
 \beta_n=\beta(q_n(h,v)),\qquad
 b=\beta_n-\widehat\beta,
\]
and, conditionally on \(\mathscr P_n\),
\[
 H_{i,ax}=\frac{\mathbf1\{X_i=x,A_i=a,R_i=1\}}
 {c_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
 (Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-\widehat\beta_{ax}).
\tag{32}
\]
The randomization and consistency assumptions identify the conditional observed outcome mean with \(\beta_{n,ax}\).  Annotation ignorability and the selected Bernoulli acquisition probability then give, coordinate by coordinate,
\[
 E(H_{i,ax}\mid\mathscr P_n)
 =\frac{c_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
 {c_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
 (\beta_{n,ax}-\widehat\beta_{ax})=b_{ax}.
\tag{33}
\]
Using the definitions of \(\widetilde\beta_n\), \(\widetilde\theta_n\), and \(\theta_p\), (33) yields the exact identities
\[
 E(\widetilde\beta_n\mid\mathscr P_n)=\beta_n,
 \qquad
 \sqrt n\{\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_p(q_n(h,v))\}
 =\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^nA_{\mathrm{map}}(H_i-b).
\tag{34}
\]

Only one coordinate of \(H_i\) is nonzero.  Its conditional second moment and (33) therefore give the exact covariance
\[
 S_n=A_{\mathrm{map}}\left[
 \operatorname{diag}_{a,x}\left\{
 \frac{\sigma^2_{ax}(q_n(h,v))+b_{ax}^2}
 {p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
 \right\}-bb^\top\right]A_{\mathrm{map}}^\top.
\tag{35}
\]
The bracketed remainder
\[
 \operatorname{diag}_{a,x}\left\{
 \frac{b_{ax}^2}{p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
 \right\}-bb^\top
\tag{36}
\]
is positive semidefinite because it is the covariance of the vector with coordinate
\(b_{ax}\mathbf1\{X=x,A=a,R=1\}/(p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax})\).

The pilot observations are bounded, the number of cells is fixed, and each cell probability \(p_xe_{ax}\) is positive.  The second-moment calculation in the proof of \(\mathrm{thm:coupled\text{-}measurable\text{-}attainment}\), now applied at the natural stochastic scale, gives
\[
 \lVert b\rVert=O_P(m_n^{-1/2})
\tag{37}
\]
locally uniformly over the fixed nuisance fiber; the event of an empty pilot cell has probability tending to zero under \(m_n\to\infty\).  Because \(q_n-q^0=s(h,v)/\sqrt n\), finiteness of the support and boundedness of \(s(h,v)\) give
\[
 \max_{a,x}|\sigma^2_{ax}(q_n(h,v))-\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)|=O(n^{-1/2})
\tag{38}
\]
uniformly on that fiber.  The \((0,x)\) and \((1,x)\) columns of \(A_{\mathrm{map}}=[-F\;F]\) are \(-p_xd_x\) and \(p_xd_x\), respectively.  Consequently
\[
 A_{\mathrm{map}}\operatorname{diag}_{a,x}\left\{
 \frac{\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)}{p_xe_{ax}r_{ax}}
 \right\}A_{\mathrm{map}}^\top
 =\sum_{x=1}^K\sum_{a=0}^1
 \frac{p_x\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)}{e_{ax}r_{ax}}d_xd_x^\top
 =\Sigma(r).
\tag{39}
\]
The fixed lower bounds on \(p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}\), (35)--(39), and \(\widehat r_n\to r^\dagger\) now imply
\[
 \lVert S_n-\Sigma(r^\dagger)\rVert
 =O_P(m_n^{-1}+n^{-1/2})+o_P(1)=o_P(1).
\tag{40}
\]
Thus the covariance remainder uses only \(m_n^{-1}\to0\).

The variance identity (1) from the coupled proof, \(q^0_{ax\ell}\ge\eta\), and two distinct support points give a positive cell-variance floor.  Together with \(\operatorname{rank}(F)=d\), equation (39) gives a common positive lower eigenvalue for \(S_n\) with probability tending to one.  The summands in (34) are uniformly bounded because \(|Y|\le C_Y\), the pilot means are clipped to the convex hull of \(\mathcal Y\), \(\widehat r_{n,ax}\ge\rho\), and \(p_xe_{ax}>0\).  After normalization by \(S_n^{-1/2}\), the sum of third Euclidean absolute moments of the \(n\) scaled summands is \(O(n^{-1/2})\).  Applying \(\mathrm{lem:bentkus\text{-}convex\text{-}set}\) and then (40) proves
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_p(q_n(h,v))\}
 \Rightarrow N(0,\Sigma(r^\dagger))
\tag{41}
\]
locally uniformly over \(h\in\mathcal H\) and \(\lVert v\rVert\le C_v\).

The established \(\mathrm{thm:local\text{-}chart\text{-}membership}\) gives
\(\sqrt n\,\theta_p(q_n(h,v))=h\).  Hence the input \(\sqrt n\,\widetilde\theta_n\) to the terminal rule converges to \(N(h,\Sigma(r^\dagger))\).  The coupled theorem chooses its rectangle count \(J_{s_n}\) with \(J_{s_n}/\sqrt n\to0\), so the convex-set error summed over its finitely many rectangles is \(o(1)\).  Its state-mesh, Gaussian-tail, quadrature, rounding, covariance, and finite-game errors also vanish.  Since \(r^\dagger\) is a minimizer of \(L\),
\[
 L(r^\dagger)=V^*,
\]
and therefore
\[
 \sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\ \lVert v\rVert\le C_v}
 E_{P_{p,q_n(h,v)},\mathcal A^*}
 [\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}(h,J_n(\mathcal A^*))]
 \le V^*+o(1).
\tag{42}
\]
The loss is bounded by \(2\sup_{h\in\mathcal H}\lVert h\rVert_\infty\), so conditional errors converging in probability may be integrated.  Taking \(\limsup_{n\to\infty}\) in (42) for fixed \(C_v\), and then \(C_v\to\infty\), gives
\[
 \mathcal R_+(\mathcal A^*)\le V^*.
\tag{43}
\]
The established \(\mathrm{thm:local\text{-}minimax\text{-}lower\text{-}bound}\) gives \(\mathcal R_-(\mathcal A)\ge V^*\) for every \(\mathcal A\in\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{det}}\).  Since \(\mathcal R_-(\mathcal A^*)\le\mathcal R_+(\mathcal A^*)\), (43) proves that the lower and upper deterministic-limit local minimax envelopes both equal \(V^*\), completing the proof.

novel.justification: An arbitrarily slowly diverging fully labelled pilot consistently estimates the finitely many bounded cell moments; together with the separate vanishing-share condition, this is sufficient for design selection, covariance stabilization, and negligible pilot information.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The pilot selector needs only finite-cell moment consistency, obtained from divergence of the pilot size. The existing separate condition that the pilot share vanishes supplies the second required limit and keeps the pilot likelihood negligible.

prose_updates.tldr: A frozen menu of overlapping policies turns prospective randomized outcome annotation into a joint decision problem because one acquired treatment--stratum outcome informs several correlated policy contrasts. The kernel derives the conditional finite-coordinate LAN experiment uniformly over a saturated finite-support outcome model and every contrast-preserving shape nuisance, characterizes the deterministic-design minimax regret value \(V^*\), gives certified computation on effectively represented inputs, and constructs a measurable nested-cell selector, joint AIPW estimator, and refined Gaussian rule attaining that value at tied, flat, disconnected, or dyadic-boundary design optima. The fully labelled pilot may diverge arbitrarily slowly provided its share vanishes: \(m_n\to\infty\) gives finite-cell moment consistency and \(m_n/n\to0\) makes its local information negligible. The selector's spatial convergence rate remains schedule- and law-specific through the positive prefix gaps. A generic continuous-objective witness shows only that continuity plus uniform objective approximation cannot yield an objective-uniform spatial recovery modulus; it is not a model-specific impossibility theorem for the Gaussian-risk family. A rational three-policy witness establishes that minimizing a scalar maximum pairwise-variance summary does not determine the Gaussian minimax-regret-optimal design: the unique optimizer of the pairwise-variance probe has regret above \(0.1965\), while a projected feasible competitor is below \(0.18453\), with separation on an explicit open neighborhood.

project_justification.gap: Existing causal annotation methods optimize scalar estimation variance, multidimensional two-phase methods optimize componentwise efficiency, and smooth policy-design theory assumes a unique curved optimum. Missing-outcome minimax-regret results instead treat exogenous incompleteness and treatment choice under partial identification; they do not choose randomized prospective annotation rates for point-identified overlapping policy loadings. None of these results combines a pilot-conditioned full-nuisance LAN transfer, correlated finite-menu regret design, nonunique deterministic selection, certified computation, and attainment with an arbitrarily slowly diverging pilot whose sample share vanishes.
project_justification.niche: The niche is prospective validation of a fixed overlapping causal-policy menu when investigators control scarce randomized follow-up, the operational objective is welfare loss from the final policy choice, and only a slowly diverging fully labelled pilot can be reserved before the main wave.
project_justification.fill: The project fills the niche with a nuisance-uniform Gaussian experiment, an exact deterministic-design minimax characterization, an effective certified solver, and a measurable tie-stable implementation requiring only \(m_n\to\infty\) and \(m_n/n\to0\). Its joint AIPW and Gaussian-rule construction attains the minimax value, while its spatial selector rate is stated honestly as schedule- and law-specific through the certified prefix-separation profile.

sampling_model.design: Two-wave prospective outcome acquisition with an independent fully labelled pilot of size \(m_n\) satisfying \(m_n\to\infty\) and \(m_n/n\to0\), followed by a pilot-measurable deterministic-rate main-wave design \(\widehat r_n\in\mathcal R_B\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The arbitrarily slowly diverging, vanishing-share pilot estimates the finitely many cell means and variances; the main wave uses the joint AIPW contrast estimator \(\widetilde\theta_n\).

prose_updates.related_work: Hirano and Porter (2009) inform the scalar fixed-experiment Gaussian decision bridge, while Masten (2023) and Kato (2026) inform finite-action Gaussian games; none observes overlapping policy loadings through selectively annotated treatment--stratum cells. Higbee (2026) proves two-wave Bayes design under a unique, strongly concave smooth policy optimum. Theorem 4 gives the theorem-level contrast required here: the rational finite menu has a three-way tie in every local decision neighborhood and fourteen contrast-preserving selective-annotation nuisance coordinates, so Higbee's uniqueness and curvature conditions do not cover the experiment. Nwankwo, Goldkind, and Zhou (2026) supply the closest scalar annotation workflow, and the Wang, Wang, and Miao preprint, listed as a FUTURE Statistica Sinica article, supplies the nearest componentwise semiparametric two-phase criterion. Levis et al. (2024) inform observed-data influence projection, Cook, Mishler, and Ramdas (2024) inform stabilized AIPW limits, and Luedtke and van der Laan (2016) identify the nonregularity of nonunique optimal decisions. Those works do not establish the present coupling of a tie-stable multivariate regret design and a discontinuous finite-policy rule under only an arbitrarily slowly diverging pilot and a vanishing pilot share; the resulting spatial rate is deliberately schedule- and law-specific. Manski (2007) studies minimax-regret treatment choice when outcomes are missing for uncontrolled reasons and the response law is partially identified. Stoye (2007) extends incomplete-data choice to many treatments, and his finite-sample missing-outcome analysis studies a fixed exogenous missing fraction. Those decision problems are important antecedents but differ from prospective randomized annotation, known propensities, point-identified policy contrasts, and optimization of the acquisition design itself. Hu et al. (2024) inform regret-sensitive allocation in separable subgroup decisions. The auxiliary functional \(G_\omega\) is introduced internally only as the geometric probe in the constructive witness. Codi et al. (2025) provide the stacked rule-comparison consumer, and Kim et al. (2025) motivate independent validation of the azithromycin rules.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The nested-cell implementation is measurable and stabilizes every fixed prefix, including separated ties, flat or disconnected minimizing sets, and dyadic-boundary minima. The resulting deterministic spatial rate \(a_n(L)\) is schedule- and law-specific because it depends on both the pilot approximation envelope and the positive prefix-separation profile of the particular objective. The displayed pair \(f_+(z)=\epsilon z\) and \(f_-(z)=\epsilon(1-z)\), both uniformly approximated by \(g(z)=\epsilon/2\), proves that continuity plus uniform objective-approximation control alone supplies no spatial recovery modulus over the generic class of continuous objectives. It does not prove that no law-uniform rate exists on the narrower Gaussian-risk family \(r\mapsto L(r)\); such a model-specific impossibility would require a separate embedding or identification-modulus argument.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The comparison class contains procedures whose fully labelled pilot sizes satisfy \(m_n\to\infty\) and \(m_n/n\to0\), and whose main-wave annotation rates converge to a deterministic feasible design; no polynomial pilot-growth condition is imposed. Fully sequential acquisition, positive-fraction pilots, bounded pilots, and random limiting designs are different experiments. The known fixed finite support has uniformly positive cell probabilities; binary or continuous clinical outcomes require a separate support formulation. Certified computation is asserted only for rational-polytopal state sets and rational or real-algebraic encoded inputs with exact certificates; no algorithmic claim covers arbitrary opaque reals or oracle-free compact sets. The certificate returns value bounds and an outer minimizer cover, while the measurable selector has a schedule- and law-specific spatial rate determined by its pilot envelope and certified prefix gaps. The generic continuous-objective counterexample rules out a recovery modulus based only on continuity and uniform objective error; it does not establish a model-specific rate impossibility for the Gaussian-risk family. The auxiliary pairwise-variance functional \(G_\omega\) is used solely as the geometric probe in the witness. The \(M=2\) proposition recovers the known Blackwell-monotone variance benchmark; new geometry begins at three overlapping policies.

statement_notes.justification: The construction gives a jointly measurable deterministic-limit selector from any diverging, vanishing-share pilot, stabilizes every fixed nested-cell prefix at nonunique and boundary optima, supplies a schedule- and law-specific spatial rate, and couples the selector to a slowly refining Gaussian rectangle rule.
statement_notes.gap: The selector rate depends jointly on the pilot schedule and the objective's certified prefix-separation profile. The proof's counterexample establishes only that generic continuity plus uniform objective-approximation control cannot yield an objective-uniform spatial recovery modulus; it makes no model-specific impossibility claim for the Gaussian-risk family.
statement_notes.consumer: This theorem supplies the implementable design and decision schedule required by the full-nuisance attainment theorem, even when the fully labelled pilot diverges arbitrarily slowly.

statement_notes.justification: The upper theorem matches the full-nuisance converse with an implementable arbitrarily slowly diverging, vanishing-share pilot, a joint estimator, and a terminal rule.
statement_notes.gap: Nwankwo et al. attain scalar ATE variance and Cook et al. prove scalar adaptive AIPW limits; neither couples a set-valued regret design to a multivariate discontinuous minimax rule under the minimal pilot limits \(m_n\to\infty\) and \(m_n/n\to0\).
statement_notes.consumer: Independent validation of a frozen clinical-policy menu can target scarce follow-up toward the cells that minimize eventual welfare loss without reserving a polynomial-order pilot.
